thread.title: Apple: U.S. iPhone Share Gains Could Boost Earnings

title: Apple: U.S. iPhone Share Gains Could Boost Earnings
text:
Signs that Apple’s smartphone market share rose in early 2018 could mean good news for its profits. 
In a Friday note, BTIG analyst Walter Piecyk reported survey data indicating that the Barron’s Next 50 company’s U.S. market share was up six-tenths of a percent to 56% from the fourth quarter, evidently “at the expense of Samsung . ” (Though since the survey data ended midmonth, it didn’t reflect the release of Samsung’s S9 .) 
Its share fell during the same period in 2017 and 2017, Piecyk noted. 
Since Apple (AAPL) introduced new high-end phones late last year, wrote Piecyk, that could be a good sign for its average iPhone selling price—which hasn’t advanced sequentially during the first calendar quarter since 2011. Illustration: BTIG 
Investors watch Apple’s average selling price closely, and some expect changes to its lineup that could keep the number moving upward; the company is in the enviable position of having both a hardware business where it can conceivably keep raising prices , and a growable services side . 
For the current quarter, BTIG expects a 6.5% dip in average selling price from the last three-month period, to $745. It projects total sales of about 52 million, down just under 33%. 
“It is still likely that legacy models are performing strongly relative to new models in the March quarter as is typically the case,” Piecyk wrote. “Nevertheless, if Apple was able to beat our ASP estimate by $10 (which still implies a 5.2% decline) it would lift revenue and EPS by $500 million and $0.02, respectively.”
